lessons.title: Cleaning the Kitchen
lessons.content_md:
# Data Wrangling 🧼

Here is the biggest secret in the Data Science industry: **Real-world data is disgusting.**

It is full of errors, missing values, duplicates, and typos. If you try to feed that dirty data into a fancy AI model, the model will fail.

Imagine you are a world-class chef about to cook a five-star meal. But when you walk into the kitchen, the countertops are covered in trash, the vegetables are rotting, and the knives are missing. You can't cook in that environment! You have to **clean the kitchen first**.

In Data Science, cleaning the kitchen is called **Data Wrangling**.

## Taking Out the Trash

Data Scientists spend up to 80% of their time just cleaning data before they ever do any "cool" analysis or machine learning.

They have to:
1. **Scrub typos:** Fixing rows where someone typed "CA" instead of "California".
2. **Fill missing holes:** Guessing the age of a user if they left the field blank (or deleting the row entirely).
3. **Remove duplicates:** Deleting accidental double-clicks that created two identical purchases in the database.

<flipcard front="🧼 What is Data Wrangling?" back="The exhausting but essential process of cleaning, structuring, and enriching raw data into a desired format for better decision making."></flipcard>

<flipcard front="🗑️ Why do we care about missing data?" back="If an algorithm tries to calculate the average age of your users, but some rows have 'NULL' (blank) for age, the math will crash and the algorithm will fail!"></flipcard>

<flipcard front="⏳ How much time does Data Wrangling take?" back="Surveys show that Data Scientists spend around 60% to 80% of their day finding, cleaning, and organizing data, rather than building fancy models."></flipcard>
